name: Judah
bio:
Judah is the fourth son of Jacob and Leah; Leah said at his birth, "Now will I praise the LORD," and named him "Judah," meaning "praise" (Genesis 29:35). When his brothers, jealous of Joseph, wanted to kill him, it was Judah who proposed selling him to a caravan of Ishmaelites instead of killing him outright, indirectly saving Joseph's life (Genesis 37:26-27); his later entanglement with his daughter-in-law Tamar, and his decisive act of offering himself in place of his brother Benjamin at the climax of Joseph's story, give his character growing complexity and depth — episodes recorded in Genesis 38 and 44 respectively.

When Jacob blessed his twelve sons on his deathbed, he singled out Judah for his brothers' praise, declaring, "The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come" — one of the most important messianic prophecies in the Old Testament. The tribe of Judah indeed went on to produce the Davidic dynasty, and ultimately Jesus Christ, called "the Lion of the tribe of Juda" (Genesis 49:8-10; Revelation 5:5).
